ECON-MG-LEGENDARY-9057.q: Refer to the graph. A report attributes the smaller market after the tax to the buyer–seller price wedge. Which quantity comparison and explanation support that account?

ECON-MG-LEGENDARY-9059.q: At Q = 80 in the tax graph, how much higher is Supply + tax than Supply, and what does this vertical distance mean?

P62B-ELAS-B1-019.q: Refer to the graph. Which total revenue at B and interpretation of a small movement in either direction along demand are correct?

P62B-ELAS-B2-019.q: Refer to the graph. As price falls from C through B to A, which total-revenue sequence and economic explanation are correct?

P62B-ELAS-B2-020.q: Use the graph. Refer to the common starting point and the higher marked price on the two supply curves. Which short-run and long-run quantity increases, and elasticity interpretation, are supported?

P62B-ELAS-E-028.q: Which demand curve is steeper in the graph, and why is that visual slope different from price elasticity of demand?

P62B-ELAS-E-029.q: Refer to the linear demand curve. Identify the price at C and classify demand as you move from C through B to A.

P62B-ELAS-EL-033.q: Refer to the graph. Which total revenue at B and interpretation of a small movement in either direction along demand are correct?

P62B-ELAS-EL-038.q: Use the graph. Refer to the common starting point and the higher marked price on the two supply curves. Which short-run and long-run quantity increases, and elasticity interpretation, are supported?

P62B-ELAS-H-016.q: The upper and lower portions of the plotted demand curve have the same slope. Which point elasticities at C and A, and explanation, reconcile that slope with different percentage responses?

P62B-ELAS-H-034.q: Refer to the linear demand graph. Which point elasticities at C and A illustrate the role of the price-to-quantity ratio in elasticity?

P62B-ELAS-M-008.q: Refer to the graph. Starting at C, which initial price and sequence of elasticity classifications describe movement down the demand curve through B to A?

P62C-CPS-B2-007.q: Refer to the graph. A student labels the price-times-quantity rectangle at E as consumer surplus. Which amount and explanation correct the mistake?

P62C-CPS-B2-008.q: Refer to the graph. A lump-sum rule transfers $20 from buyers to sellers without changing quantity, allocation or resource costs. What is producer surplus after the transfer, and what happens to total surplus?

P62C-CPS-B2-009.q: Refer to the graph. A report adds sales revenue at E to consumer and producer surplus when measuring total gains from exchange. Which total and diagnosis are correct?

Total surplus is $80; sales revenue should be added because it is an additional gain.

P62C-CPS-B2-010.q: Refer to the graph. A quota limits production to four units, allocated to the highest-value buyers and lowest-cost sellers. What gain would removing the quota create, and why?

P62C-CPS-EL-017.q: Refer to the graph. A seller claims that its revenue at E measures its producer surplus. Which calculation and explanation evaluate the claim?

Revenue = $72 and producer surplus = $0; the $72 payment itself is the seller’s gain above resource cost.
Revenue = $60 and producer surplus = $0; the $60 payment itself is the seller’s gain above resource cost.

P62C-CPS-H-005.q: Refer to the graph. Which amount and region represent consumer surplus at E?

P62C-CPS-H-007.q: Refer to the graph. At E, what is total surplus, and how does it differ from buyer expenditure?

$40; it measures value above resource cost, while expenditure is a payment.

P62C-CPS-L-020.q: Refer to the graph. A student argues that the allocation at E is efficient only if buyers and sellers receive equal surplus. Which quantity and explanation correctly evaluate this claim under the standard competitive assumptions?

P62C-CPS-L-024.q: Refer to the graph. A student argues that the allocation at E is efficient only if buyers and sellers receive equal surplus. Which quantity and explanation correctly evaluate this claim under the standard competitive assumptions?
options: 6 units: marginal willingness to pay equals marginal cost; equal surplus shares are not required.

P62C-CPS-L-028.q: Refer to the graph. A student argues that the allocation at E is efficient only if buyers and sellers receive equal surplus. Which quantity and explanation correctly evaluate this claim under the standard competitive assumptions?

P62C-CPS-L-029.q: Refer to the graph. Output is held at the vertical line through A and B. Which marginal comparison supports expanding output toward E?

P62C-CPS-L-030.q: Refer to the graph. Repealing the restriction at the marked quantity left of E restores E and transfers $9 from producers to consumers on continuing trades. Assuming efficient allocation and no other effects, which total-surplus change and explanation are correct?

P62C-CPS-L-031.q: Refer to the graph. Output is held at the vertical line through A and B. Which marginal comparison supports reducing output toward the competitive quantity?
options: At that output, value is $6 and cost is $10; reducing the units with cost above value raises total surplus.

At that output, value is $8 and cost is $12; reducing the units with cost above value raises total surplus.

P62C-CPS-LB-010.q: Refer to the graph. A proposal would redistribute surplus solely because the current buyer and seller shares differ. Which calculation and efficiency judgment evaluate that justification?
options: CS = $48 and PS = $24; unequal shares alone do not establish inefficiency.

CS = $48 and PS = $24; unequal shares alone establish inefficiency.
CS = $64 and PS = $32; unequal shares alone do not establish inefficiency.

P62C-CPS-LB-011.q: Refer to the graph. A student uses the surplus shares at E to argue that every efficient market must divide its gains equally. Which reading and judgment are correct?

CS and PS are each $20; their equality here does not establish a general efficiency requirement.
CS and PS are each $25; their equality here establishes a general efficiency requirement.

P62C-CPS-LB-012.q: Refer to the graph. Starting at the marked quantity through A and B, what change in total surplus would expanding output to E cause, and why?

P62C-CPS-LB-013.q: Refer to the graph. Starting at the marked quantity through A and B, what change in total surplus would reducing output to E cause, and why?

A $4 gain: the change transfers that amount from sellers to buyers.

options: About $6 per unit; the same fixed cost is spread over more units.
About $12 per unit; the same fixed cost is spread over more units.
About $12 per unit; this is the extra cost of the next unit, so a smaller gap means lower MC.
About $12 per unit; it remains $12 at Q = 70 because total fixed cost is unchanged.
P62E-COP-L-054.feedback: At Q = 20 the gap and the AFC curve are about $12; by Q = 70 they are about $3.4. The gap is AFC = TFC/Q. With TFC = $240 unchanged, a larger denominator reduces fixed cost per unit.

P62E-COP-L-057.q: Refer to the TP graph. The firm hires an eighth worker at a positive wage. Which output change and production implication follow?
options: Output falls from 62 to 60; this hire cannot be a way to produce additional output.
Output falls from 64 to 62; this hire cannot be a way to produce additional output.
Output falls from 62 to 60; the positive wage ensures that this hire increases output.
Output falls from 64 to 62; the positive wage ensures that this hire increases output.
P62E-COP-L-057.feedback: TP falls from 62 at seven workers to 60 at eight, so the eighth worker has MP = −2. Paying more for labor on this segment lowers rather than expands production.

P62E-COP-L-058.q: Refer to the LRATC graph. Between which outputs is average cost constant, and how should the regions on either side be interpreted?
options: About 30 to 60; economies of scale precede this interval and diseconomies follow it.
About 45 to 80; economies of scale precede this interval and diseconomies follow it.
About 45 to 80; diseconomies of scale precede this interval and economies follow it.
About 30 to 60; diseconomies of scale precede this interval and economies follow it.
P62E-COP-L-058.feedback: LRATC falls until about Q = 45, is flat through Q = 80, then rises. Falling, constant and rising long-run average cost represent economies, constant returns and diseconomies of scale, respectively.

P62E-COP-L-059.q: Refer to the LRATC graph. What output is marked, and what does it represent for the firm’s scale?
options: 80 units; minimum efficient scale.
60 units; the largest output the firm is technologically able to produce.
60 units; minimum efficient scale.
80 units; the largest output the firm is technologically able to produce.
P62E-COP-L-059.feedback: The marker is at Q = 60, the lowest point of LRATC. Minimum efficient scale is the smallest output attaining minimum long-run average cost; it is not a technological capacity ceiling.

P62E-COP-L-060.q: Refer to the plant-cost graph. At Q = 75, which available plant has the lowest average cost, and how should a firm able to choose its plant use that comparison?
options: Plant 2; choose the lowest available plant cost at the required output.
Plant 3; average all three plant costs to find the cost of the best plant.
Plant 2; average all three plant costs to find the cost of the best plant.
Plant 3; choose the lowest available plant cost at the required output.
P62E-COP-L-060.feedback: At Q = 75, SRATC3 lies below SRATC2 and SRATC1. The least-cost plant choice uses the minimum available cost at that output, not the mean of plant costs.

P62E-COP-L-091.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 40, which ordering holds, and what does it imply about a small increase in output?
options: MC < AVC < AC; the next units cost less than either average, lowering both AVC and AC.
AVC < MC < AC; the next units cost more than AVC but less than AC, lowering AVC and raising AC.
MC < AVC < AC; the next units cost less than either average, raising both AVC and AC.
AVC < MC < AC; the next units cost more than AVC but less than AC, raising AVC and lowering AC.
P62E-COP-L-091.feedback: At Q = 40, MC lies above AVC but below AC. A marginal cost above an average pulls that average up; a marginal cost below an average pulls it down. Thus AVC rises and AC falls.

P62E-COP-L-095.q: A firm adds one worker beyond the total-product maximum in the graph. Which worker is this, and what can be inferred about marginal and average product?
options: The 13th worker; MP is negative but AP remains positive.
The 11th worker; both MP and AP must be negative.
The 11th worker; MP is negative but AP remains positive.
The 13th worker; both MP and AP must be negative.
P62E-COP-L-095.feedback: TP peaks at 10 workers. The 11th worker lowers TP, giving negative MP, but TP remains positive. AP = TP/L therefore remains positive. Marginal and average product need not have the same sign.

P62E-COP-M-021.q: Refer to the TP graph. Compare the contributions of the fifth and sixth workers. Which changes and production interpretation are correct?
options: They add 12 and 10 units; TP rises at a decreasing rate.
They add 10 and 8 units; diminishing MP means TP falls.
They add 10 and 8 units; TP rises at a decreasing rate.
They add 12 and 10 units; diminishing MP means TP falls.
P62E-COP-M-021.feedback: TP at four, five and six workers is 46, 56 and 64. The marginal products are 10 and 8. They remain positive but decrease, so TP continues rising more slowly.

P62E-COP-M-024.q: Refer to the graph. What is the vertical difference between total cost and total variable cost, and why does it remain at that amount as output changes?
options: $120 of total fixed cost; TC equals TVC plus this constant amount.
$240 of total fixed cost; TC equals TVC plus this constant amount.
$240 of total fixed cost; this amount must be added again for each additional unit produced.
$0 of fixed cost, because TC and TVC rise by the same amount when output changes.
P62E-COP-M-024.feedback: The horizontal fixed-cost line is at $240. TC starts at $240 while TVC starts at zero. Their difference is $240 at every output because TC = TVC+TFC. This is a total, not a marginal or per-unit cost.

P62E-COP-M-026.q: Refer to the graph. Where does MC cross AVC, and what do the marginal-average relationships imply at the crossing?
options: At roughly Q = 25; the next units switch from lowering to raising the relevant average because MC crosses it from below.
At roughly Q = 32; the next units switch from raising to lowering the relevant average because MC crosses it from below.
At roughly Q = 25; the next units switch from raising to lowering the relevant average because MC crosses it from below.
At roughly Q = 32; the next units switch from lowering to raising the relevant average because MC crosses it from below.
P62E-COP-M-026.feedback: MC crosses AVC at roughly Q = 32. Before each crossing MC is below that average and pulls it down; after the crossing MC is above it and pulls it up. Thus the crossing identifies a minimum, not a maximum.

P62F-PC-B1-005.q: Use the graph. Which approximate quantity at Q1 and marginal condition identify the firm’s profit-maximizing output?
options: About 40 units; MC rises through price, so extra units beyond it cost more than they add to revenue.
About 60 units; any MC = price crossing is equally profit maximizing regardless of the direction of crossing.
About 60 units; MC rises through price, so extra units beyond it cost more than they add to revenue.
About 40 units; any MC = price crossing is equally profit maximizing regardless of the direction of crossing.
P62F-PC-B1-005.feedback: Q1 is near 60 on rising MC. Just below it MR = P exceeds MC; just above it MC exceeds MR. This change in marginal profit identifies a maximum, unlike a falling-MC crossing.

P62F-PC-B1-019.q: At the profit-maximizing output in the graph, what is profit per unit, and which comparison measures it?
options: $15, from price minus ATC.
$10, from price minus AVC.
$15, from price minus AVC.
$10, from price minus ATC.
P62F-PC-B1-019.feedback: Rising MC meets price at Q = 50. Price is $30, ATC $20 and AVC $10. Profit per unit is P−ATC = $10; P−AVC instead measures contribution toward fixed cost.

P62F-PC-B1-020.q: Refer to the graph. Which price and price–cost comparison establish that the firm breaks even at its profit-maximizing output?
options: $20; P = ATC gives zero economic profit while covering the normal return included in economic cost.
$25; P = ATC gives zero economic profit while covering the normal return included in economic cost.
$25; P = ATC means the owner’s opportunity cost and normal return are not covered.
$20; P = ATC means the owner’s opportunity cost and normal return are not covered.
P62F-PC-B1-020.feedback: The firm chooses Q = 50 at P = MC = 25, and ATC is also 25. Revenue covers all economic costs, including implicit opportunity costs; zero economic profit is break-even, not no return.

P62F-PC-B2-024.q: At Q1 in the graph, what is the approximate height of the profit rectangle, and what does that height measure?
options: between $6 and $10 per unit; price minus ATC measures economic profit per unit.
between $10 and $15 per unit; price minus ATC measures economic profit per unit.
between $10 and $15 per unit; the vertical gap alone is total economic profit.
between $6 and $10 per unit; the vertical gap alone is total economic profit.
P62F-PC-B2-024.feedback: At Q1, the price–ATC gap is about 13–14 dollars. The height is price minus ATC, an amount per unit. Multiply it by Q1 to obtain total profit.

P62F-PC-B2-025.q: At Q1 in the graph, what is the approximate height of the loss rectangle, and what does that height measure?
options: between $6 and $10 per unit; ATC minus price measures economic loss per unit.
between $4 and $6 per unit; the vertical gap alone is total economic loss.
between $4 and $6 per unit; ATC minus price measures economic loss per unit.
between $6 and $10 per unit; the vertical gap alone is total economic loss.
P62F-PC-B2-025.feedback: At Q1, price is 20 and ATC around 25. The height is ATC minus price, an amount per unit. Multiply it by Q1 to obtain total loss.

P62F-PC-B2-036.q: What is the approximate shutdown-price threshold in the graph, and which part of MC supplies the firm’s positive short-run output?
options: $22; rising MC at and above minimum AVC.
$18; rising MC at and above minimum AVC.
$18; the entire MC curve, including prices below minimum AVC.
$22; the entire MC curve, including prices below minimum AVC.
P62F-PC-B2-036.feedback: The AVC minimum is about 18, where rising MC meets it. Above this price the firm selects rising MC = P. Below it no positive output covers variable cost, so that lower MC segment is not operating supply.

P62F-PC-B2-037.q: Which operating loss and shutdown loss are implied by the graph, and what should the firm do if fixed cost is unavoidable?
options: Operate: lose $200; shut down: lose $500. Producing covers variable cost and part of fixed cost.
Operate: lose $300; shut down: lose $600. Producing covers variable cost and part of fixed cost.
Operate: lose $300; shut down: lose $600. A loss alone requires shutdown regardless of the avoidable-cost comparison.
Operate: lose $200; shut down: lose $500. A loss alone requires shutdown regardless of the avoidable-cost comparison.
P62F-PC-B2-037.feedback: At Q = 30, P = 30, ATC = 40 and AVC = 20. Operating loss = (40−30) × 30 = 300; fixed cost = (40−20) × 30 = 600. Production contributes (30−20) × 30 = 300 toward that unavoidable cost, reducing the loss.

P62F-PC-B3-055.q: Use the graph. Starting with the market panel, which firm output and analysis correctly determine the representative firm’s current outcome?
options: 75 units; take market price as MR, use rising MC = MR, then compare price with ATC.
90 units; take market quantity as firm output and compare price with MC to measure total profit.
90 units; take market price as MR, use rising MC = MR, then compare price with ATC.
75 units; take market quantity as firm output and compare price with MC to measure total profit.
P62F-PC-B3-055.feedback: Market price is 40. In the firm panel this horizontal MR meets rising MC at 90. ATC is 20 there, so the subsequent profit comparison uses price minus ATC, not the market quantity or the MC gap.

P62F-PC-B3-056.q: Use the paired market and firm diagram. Under free entry with identical firms and unchanged input prices and cost curves, which current profit and eventual market adjustment eliminate the incentive to enter?
options: $1,500; entry expands market supply, lowering price and each firm’s output along rising MC until economic profit is zero.
$1,800; entry reduces market supply and raises each survivor’s price and output until profit is zero.
$1,500; entry reduces market supply and raises each survivor’s price and output until profit is zero.
$1,800; entry expands market supply, lowering price and each firm’s output along rising MC until economic profit is zero.
P62F-PC-B3-056.feedback: The market sets P = 40. The firm chooses Q = 90, with ATC = 20, earning (40−20) × 90 = 1800. Entry adds market supply and lowers the shared price. Each firm’s MR falls and its output contracts along fixed rising MC. Under the stated conditions adjustment ends at P = MC = minimum ATC.

P62F-PC-B3-057.q: Use the paired market and firm diagram to compare the firm’s revenue, variable cost and total cost. Which operating loss and decisions distinguish the short run from the long run?
options: $100; operate because P > AVC, while persistent losses lead to exit and higher market price.
$150; operate because P > AVC, while persistent losses lead to exit and higher market price.
$150; shut down immediately because P < ATC, even though producing covers avoidable cost.
$100; shut down immediately because P < ATC, even though producing covers avoidable cost.
P62F-PC-B3-057.feedback: The market sets P = 15; rising MC gives Q = 50. AVC = 10 < P = 15 < ATC = 18, so the operating loss is 150 and shutdown would sacrifice a contribution to fixed cost. Persistent losses induce exit and raise price as market supply contracts.

P62F-PC-B3-058.q: Starting with market price in the paired market and firm diagram, which firm output and cost relationships summarize the long-run competitive equilibrium?
options: P = $20, Q = 40; P = MC = minimum ATC gives zero economic profit and no net entry or exit pressure.
P = $25, Q = 50; P = AVC alone establishes long-run break-even and removes all entry or exit pressure.
P = $20, Q = 40; P = AVC alone establishes long-run break-even and removes all entry or exit pressure.
P = $25, Q = 50; P = MC = minimum ATC gives zero economic profit and no net entry or exit pressure.
P62F-PC-B3-058.feedback: The market supplies price 25 to the firm. Its rising MC crosses at Q = 50, also the ATC minimum. P = MC gives marginal efficiency; P = min ATC gives productive efficiency and zero economic profit. Covering AVC alone is only a short-run operating criterion.

P62F-PC-EL-012.q: The cost curves shown include a per-unit tax. Which market price and assessment of the firm’s taxed short-run decision are correct?
options: $10; shut down because the tax-adjusted AVC minimum is above price.
$14; keep producing because a per-unit tax is fixed cost and cannot affect the shutdown threshold.
$10; keep producing because a per-unit tax is fixed cost and cannot affect the shutdown threshold.
$14; shut down because the tax-adjusted AVC minimum is above price.
P62F-PC-EL-012.feedback: The plotted price is 14, below the taxed AVC minimum near 19. A tax paid per unit enters avoidable costs and can raise the operating threshold. It is not a lump-sum fixed charge.

P62F-PC-EL-018.q: Use the graph. Market price rises from the level plotted while the firm’s cost curves stay fixed. Which starting price range and changes on the firm panel are correct?
options: Between $30 and $35; the horizontal P = MR line rises and output increases along unchanged MC.
Between $40 and $45; the horizontal P = MR line rises and output increases along unchanged MC.
Between $40 and $45; the price increase itself shifts the firm’s MC curve upward.
Between $30 and $35; the price increase itself shifts the firm’s MC curve upward.
P62F-PC-EL-018.feedback: The current price is slightly above 40. A higher market price raises the firm’s horizontal revenue line; its rising MC crossing moves right. With costs held fixed, MC does not shift.

P62F-PC-EL-033.q: At the chosen output, what is the price–AVC margin, and why does the graph show break-even rather than the shutdown threshold?
options: $5; price equals ATC and exceeds AVC, covering all economic costs.
$10; zero economic profit means price must equal minimum AVC.
$10; price equals ATC and exceeds AVC, covering all economic costs.
$5; zero economic profit means price must equal minimum AVC.
P62F-PC-EL-033.feedback: At Q = 50, P = ATC = 25 and AVC = 15, leaving 10 above variable cost per unit. The firm covers all economic costs. Shutdown indifference occurs at minimum AVC, not at zero economic profit.

P62F-PC-EL-034.q: Which operating loss and shutdown loss are implied by the graph, and what should the firm do if fixed cost is unavoidable?
options: Operate: lose $200; shut down: lose $500. Producing covers variable cost and part of fixed cost.
Operate: lose $300; shut down: lose $600. A loss alone requires shutdown regardless of the avoidable-cost comparison.
Operate: lose $300; shut down: lose $600. Producing covers variable cost and part of fixed cost.
Operate: lose $200; shut down: lose $500. A loss alone requires shutdown regardless of the avoidable-cost comparison.
P62F-PC-EL-034.feedback: At Q = 30, P = 30, ATC = 40 and AVC = 20. Operating loss = (40−30) × 30 = 300; fixed cost = (40−20) × 30 = 600. Production contributes (30−20) × 30 = 300 toward that unavoidable cost, reducing the loss.

P62F-PC-EL-036.q: At what price does the positive-output portion of short-run supply begin in the graph, and why is lower MC excluded?
options: $30 at B; lower prices do not cover minimum AVC.
$20 at A; lower prices do not cover minimum AVC.
$20 at A; any positive MC guarantees that producing covers total cost.
$30 at B; any positive MC guarantees that producing covers total cost.
P62F-PC-EL-036.feedback: A is at price 20 and the minimum of AVC. The rising MC segment from there gives operating supply. Below 20, a possible MC crossing is insufficient because revenue cannot cover variable cost.

P62F-PC-EL-037.q: Use the graph. Fixed cost falls while MC and AVC remain as drawn. What happens to the shutdown price, and why?
options: It remains $30; minimum AVC, not fixed cost, sets the operating threshold.
It remains $20; fixed cost is the avoidable cost that determines shutdown.
It remains $20; minimum AVC, not fixed cost, sets the operating threshold.
It remains $30; fixed cost is the avoidable cost that determines shutdown.
P62F-PC-EL-037.feedback: Minimum AVC is 20 at A. Lower fixed cost reduces ATC and affects economic profit, but unchanged AVC and MC leave the shutdown threshold at 20.

P62F-PC-EL-038.q: Use the paired market and firm diagram. Assume free entry, identical firms and unchanged input prices and cost curves. Which current profit and subsequent changes in market supply, firm MR and firm output describe the path to long-run equilibrium?
options: $1,500; entry expands market supply, lowering price and each firm’s output along rising MC until economic profit is zero.
$1,800; entry lowers market price, but an incumbent’s MR stays at its original level because that firm is a price taker.
$1,800; entry expands market supply, lowering price and each firm’s output along rising MC until economic profit is zero.
$3,600; entry expands supply and lowers price until this sales revenue is zero.
P62F-PC-EL-038.feedback: At P = $40, Q = 90 and ATC = $20, profit is $1,800; revenue is $3,600. Entry expands market supply and lowers the price faced by each price-taking firm. Firm MR falls and output contracts along rising MC until P = minimum ATC and economic profit is zero.

P62F-PC-EL-039.q: Use the graph. Which plotted market and firm quantities and interpretation respect the difference between the panels?
options: Market 100 thousand, firm 80; the market total and one firm’s output use different aggregation levels and scales.
Market 75 thousand, firm 90; market quantity must be assigned to each firm because both face the same price.
Market 100 thousand, firm 80; market quantity must be assigned to each firm because both face the same price.
Market 75 thousand, firm 90; the market total and one firm’s output use different aggregation levels and scales.
P62F-PC-EL-039.feedback: The left equilibrium is 75 on a thousands scale, while the right panel’s rising MC crossing is 90 firm units. Price 40 links the panels, but their quantity axes describe different economic objects.

P62F-PC-EL-040.q: As exit raises market price with the surviving firm’s costs fixed, which initial quantity and output response are supported by the graph?
options: 50 units; the higher horizontal MR line selects more output on rising MC.
40 units; the higher horizontal MR line selects more output on rising MC.
50 units; the price increase shifts MC rather than changing the chosen point on it.
40 units; the price increase shifts MC rather than changing the chosen point on it.
P62F-PC-EL-040.feedback: The initial firm output is 50 at P = 15. A higher price raises MR = P and moves its intersection rightward on the unchanged rising MC curve. The firm expands output; its cost schedule does not shift.

P62F-PC-EL-042.q: Use the graph. Which market and firm quantities are plotted, and why is dividing them insufficient to establish an exact firm count?
options: 100 thousand and 40; an exact count also requires compatible units and evidence that firms have identical output.
75 thousand and 50; a representative-firm drawing by itself proves every firm has that identical output.
75 thousand and 50; an exact count also requires compatible units and evidence that firms have identical output.
100 thousand and 40; a representative-firm drawing by itself proves every firm has that identical output.
P62F-PC-EL-042.feedback: The market panel shows 75 on a thousands axis and the firm panel shows 50. Although price links the panels, an exact firm count requires knowing that the firm quantity uses compatible units and that every active firm produces that amount. The drawing alone does not supply those assumptions.

P62F-PC-EL-043.q: Use the graph. How do the two panels determine the representative firm’s price and output?
options: The market sets price at about $20; the firm takes it as horizontal MR and selects output on rising MC.
The market sets price at about $25; the firm takes it as horizontal MR and selects output on rising MC.
The market sets price at about $25; the firm uses the whole market quantity as its own output regardless of MC.
The market sets price at about $20; the firm uses the whole market quantity as its own output regardless of MC.
P62F-PC-EL-043.feedback: Market supply and demand meet at price about 25. That price becomes the individual price taker’s P = MR = AR line. The firm uses its own rising MC to choose output; aggregate market quantity is not assigned to each firm.

P62F-PC-EL-044.q: Which price and firm output in the paired market and firm diagram, together with the economic conditions, establish a long-run competitive benchmark rather than only current break-even?
options: P = $20, Q = 40; P = MC = minimum ATC gives zero economic profit and no net entry or exit pressure.
P = $25, Q = 50; zero economic profit means the firm covers explicit costs but cannot cover the owners’ opportunity costs.
P = $25, Q = 50; P = MC = minimum ATC gives zero economic profit and no net entry or exit pressure.
P = $25, Q = 50; P = MC alone rules out further entry even when P exceeds ATC.
P62F-PC-EL-044.feedback: The market supplies price 25 to the firm. Its rising MC crosses at Q = 50, also the ATC minimum. P = MC gives marginal efficiency; P = min ATC gives productive efficiency and zero economic profit. Covering AVC alone is only a short-run operating criterion.

P62F-PC-H-011.q: Use the graph. Which price reading and order of analysis correctly determine the firm’s output and profit?
options: Price is between $35 and $40; use rising MC = P to choose output, then compare P with ATC there.
Price is between $40 and $45; use rising MC = P to choose output, then compare P with ATC there.
Price is between $35 and $40; choose minimum ATC first regardless of the price–MC intersection.
Price is between $40 and $45; choose minimum ATC first regardless of the price–MC intersection.
P62F-PC-H-011.feedback: The price line is near 37. It crosses rising MC at Q1 to the right of minimum ATC. At Q1 price exceeds ATC, giving a profit rectangle (P−ATC)Q1. Average-cost minimization is not the general output rule.

P62F-PC-H-012.q: Which market price and short-run decision are supported by the graph?
options: $22; produce at the rising-MC intersection despite an economic loss because price covers AVC.
$20; produce at the rising-MC intersection despite an economic loss because price covers AVC.
$20; shut down because price below ATC is sufficient for shutdown.
$22; shut down because price below ATC is sufficient for shutdown.
P62F-PC-H-012.feedback: The horizontal price is 20, between AVC and ATC at Q1. Revenue covers variable cost and contributes toward fixed cost, making production less costly than shutdown even though economic profit is negative.

P62F-PC-H-013.q: Which price reading and operating decision are supported by the graph?
options: $10; shut down because price is below minimum AVC, bearing unavoidable fixed cost.
$14; produce at a price–MC crossing even though no positive output covers variable cost.
$14; shut down because price is below minimum AVC, bearing unavoidable fixed cost.
$10; produce at a price–MC crossing even though no positive output covers variable cost.
P62F-PC-H-013.feedback: The price line is 14, below minimum AVC near 19. At any positive output revenue fails to cover variable cost. Shutdown avoids that extra loss, but fixed cost remains.

P62F-PC-H-014.q: At the price shown, which profit and productive-efficiency conclusions follow from the firm’s cost curves?
options: $28; P = MC = minimum ATC gives zero economic profit, normal return and productive efficiency.
$23; zero economic profit leaves normal return uncovered, and output at minimum ATC is productively inefficient.
$28; zero economic profit leaves normal return uncovered, and output at minimum ATC is productively inefficient.
$23; P = MC = minimum ATC gives zero economic profit, normal return and productive efficiency.
P62F-PC-H-014.feedback: The price line is near 23 and passes through the ATC minimum and rising MC at Q1. The firm covers explicit and implicit economic costs at minimum average cost, giving normal return with zero economic profit. The selected output is at minimum ATC, so it also achieves productive efficiency.

P62F-PC-H-015.q: Suppose the plotted outcome followed higher buyer demand from an initial zero-profit equilibrium, before entry and with firm costs unchanged. What price range does the graph show, and how does the higher market price affect the firm’s revenue, output, and profit?
options: Between $40 and $50; higher market price raises the firm’s horizontal MR, expands output along MC and creates short-run profit.
Between $30 and $40; higher market price raises the firm’s horizontal MR, expands output along MC and creates short-run profit.
Between $40 and $50; higher buyer demand shifts the individual firm’s MC upward while leaving its MR fixed.
Between $30 and $40; higher buyer demand shifts the individual firm’s MC upward while leaving its MR fixed.
P62F-PC-H-015.feedback: The market price near 45 appears as the firm’s horizontal revenue line above ATC at its rising MC crossing. Relative to initial zero profit, the higher price raises MR and chosen output without shifting costs, allowing short-run profit before entry.

P62F-PC-H-016.q: Use the graph. Which approximate quantity at Q1 and marginal condition identify the firm’s profit-maximizing output?
options: About 40 units; MC rises through price, so extra units beyond it cost more than they add to revenue.
About 60 units; MC rises through price, so extra units beyond it cost more than they add to revenue.
About 60 units; any MC = price crossing is equally profit maximizing regardless of the direction of crossing.
About 40 units; any MC = price crossing is equally profit maximizing regardless of the direction of crossing.
P62F-PC-H-016.feedback: Q1 is near 60 on rising MC. Just below it MR = P exceeds MC; just above it MC exceeds MR. This change in marginal profit identifies a maximum, unlike a falling-MC crossing.

P62F-PC-H-017.q: What is the approximate shutdown-price threshold in the graph, and which part of MC supplies the firm’s positive short-run output?
options: $20; rising MC at and above minimum AVC.
$16; the entire MC curve, including prices below minimum AVC.
$16; rising MC at and above minimum AVC.
$20; the entire MC curve, including prices below minimum AVC.
P62F-PC-H-017.feedback: The AVC minimum is about 16, where rising MC meets it. Above this price the firm selects rising MC = P. Below it no positive output covers variable cost, so that lower MC segment is not operating supply.

P62F-PC-H-018.q: Use the graph. Which approximate final price P2 and explanation of the long-run adjustment are correct?
options: $30; entry expands supply and lowers price until positive economic profit disappears.
$25; entry stops only when the market price is zero.
$30; entry stops only when the market price is zero.
$25; entry expands supply and lowers price until positive economic profit disappears.
P62F-PC-H-018.feedback: The dashed final firm price P2 is near 25 at the ATC minimum. Initially P1 is above ATC at the firm’s optimum, attracting entry. Entry expands supply and lowers price until positive economic profit disappears. Zero economic profit covers normal return.

P62F-PC-H-019.q: Use the graph. Which approximate final price P2 and explanation of the long-run adjustment are correct?
options: $25; exit reduces supply and raises price until economic losses disappear.
$30; exit reduces supply and raises price until economic losses disappear.
$25; exit stops only when all firms have shut down.
$30; exit stops only when all firms have shut down.
P62F-PC-H-019.feedback: The dashed final firm price P2 is near 25 at the ATC minimum. Initially P1 is below ATC at the firm’s optimum, prompting exit. Exit reduces supply and raises price until economic losses disappear. Zero economic profit covers normal return.

P62F-PC-H-038.q: If market price rises to the level at B in the graph, which output and rule apply?
options: About 44 units; choose rising MC equal to price, since that price is above minimum AVC.
About 36 units; choose the minimum of ATC independently of the market price.
About 44 units; choose the minimum of ATC independently of the market price.
